excerpt: A wrong police report can sink a claim. How to get a Georgia crash report corrected, and what to do when the officer will not amend it.
keyTakeaways: Request a copy of your crash report right away: GDOT, the statewide custodian, sells Georgia crash reports through BuyCrash or by mail for $5 ($2 more for a certified copy), and Savannah Police also fill requests directly. For a clerical error such as a wrong plate number or misspelled name, contact the investigating officer with a document that shows the correct detail. Only the investigating officer and agency can amend a Georgia crash report, and they will not rewrite a conclusion about fault simply because a driver disagrees with it. If the officer will not change it, write a concise, factual, signed and dated account and give it to your attorney. Fault errors cost money: under O.C.G.A. § 51-12-33 you recover nothing if you are 50 percent or more at fault, and your damages are reduced by any smaller share. Georgia law requires the driver to notify police immediately of a crash involving injury, death, or apparent property damage of $500 or more (O.C.G.A. § 40-6-273).

faqs.question: Why does an error in my police report matter?
faqs.answer: Because insurers rely heavily on the report. If the details are wrong it could cause problems for any claim you pursue, particularly where the error touches on who caused the collision.

faqs.question: What kinds of errors appear in police reports?
faqs.answer: Factual mistakes such as wrong vehicle or location details, facts from your statement recorded incorrectly or left out entirely, and disputed errors where the officer's conclusion is contested rather than simply mistaken.

faqs.question: How do I get mistakes removed from a police report?
faqs.answer: Obtain a copy first, then contact the reporting agency with the specific correction and any supporting evidence. Factual errors are usually easier to amend than an officer's stated conclusion about fault.

faqs.question: Why does a fault error matter so much in Georgia?
faqs.answer: Because Georgia applies a modified comparative negligence rule (O.C.G.A. § 51-12-33): how fault is apportioned directly reduces what you recover, and at 50 percent or more you recover nothing. An error that inflates your share costs you real money.

faqs.question: Are police reports required in Georgia?
faqs.answer: Georgia law requires the driver to notify police immediately after any crash involving injury, death, or apparent property damage of $500 or more (O.C.G.A. § 40-6-273), and reporting is advisable in almost all others. Without a report you have no neutral record of the collision to support your claim when accounts later diverge.
